description:
How 240,000 Nvidia chips, $77.5 billion of them, got into China after America banned them.

Make videos like this with the app we use: madeovernight.com

We make every video on this channel with a studio called Overnight, and they've just opened their app to the public. You give it an idea, and it researches, writes, voices and builds the whole video, with sound and music, on your own Mac or PC. It's usually $127 a month and right now it's $77. The price goes up as more people join, and at 300 members it closes to the public again. 
LINK: madeovernight.com

Alice Huang is a Chinese spy who met Jensen Huang through her husband, a Shanghai fund manager who knew him from investing in video game companies. A Shanghai company tied to her family, Shanghai Century Litong, became a preferred Nvidia partner four months after it opened, and chips billed to her Singapore company, Megaspeed, went to data centers in Malaysia, where Chinese companies were allowed to rent them, and on to Shanghai. American inspectors found unopened Nvidia servers at Megaspeed's sites, and Washington added no new name to its blacklist for thirteen months.

Should Nvidia be allowed to sell its chips to China?
